clue.text: I don't think a lot can be changed

definitions.text: I don't think a lot can be changed

parts.words: I don't think a lot can be changed
parts.note: surface reading: someone saying they are not convinced much can be altered
setter's reading: one's lot is one's fate, and this person believes that destiny is fixed and cannot be altered

explanation.surface: A weary sceptic shrugs that very little in the world can ever really change.
explanation.walkthrough: A lot here is not 'much' but your lot in life, your fate; a FATALIST believes fate is fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who believes events are predetermined and beyond human control speaks exactly this sentence.

indicators.note: the conflict is placed in the hospital department's letters, which wrap around it

parts.note: the letters A and E, the outer layer
conflict between nations is war

explanation.surface: Someone notices fighting breaking out in a hospital emergency department.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E (Accident and Emergency) is the British name for a hospital emergency room; here it just supplies the letters A and E around WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To be aware is to be conscious, both adjectives meaning knowing or perceiving something.

indicators.note: something given in speech is heard rather than read, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: an old salt is a seasoned sailor, so a sailor is a salt

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of verbally attacking a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: An assault is a violent attack, and as a verb it means to attack physically.

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so only every other letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of kitchen

explanation.surface: An instruction to put something in the kitchen freezer now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: To ice something is to chill or freeze it, and frozen water is the noun.

clue.text: It's become apparent priest ran off

definitions.note: the clue gives a whole clause, 'it transpires', while the answer is the bare verb

indicators.note: off as in gone wrong or spoiled, so the letters before it are out of their proper order

parts.note: the letters of both words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: It has emerged that a clergyman has fled the parish.
explanation.definitionFit: When a fact transpires it comes to light or turns out to be true, the sense of becoming apparent.

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to have someone is to fool them, so deceived is had

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie was conned while travelling in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Chad is a landlocked nation in north-central Africa bordering Libya, Niger and Sudan.

indicators.note: one thing placed inside another is in it, so the abbreviation for the state wraps around

parts.note: Cal is a common abbreviation for California
R is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a run
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A woman is knocked down by a car somewhere in California.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls and a run is a point scored; both have one-letter abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Carol is a female given name, so a woman can be one example of it.

parts.note: taken as written
T is the symbol for the tesla, the SI unit of magnetic flux density
a problem or concern is an issue

explanation.surface: A fault with a Tesla electric car is being debated.
explanation.walkthrough: Tesla looks like the car maker, but it is the unit of magnetic field strength, abbreviated T.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter at issue is the point being debated or considered, so the phrase means under discussion.

clue.text: Young girl's fib taking in fool

indicators.note: taking in means admitting something inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a fib is a small lie
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A child's small untruth involves tricking somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassie is the Scottish and northern English word for a girl or young woman.

clue.text: Fearful of an attack on female

indicators.note: in an across clue 'X on Y' places X after Y, so the attack follows the female

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, a
F is the standard abbreviation for female
a raid is a surprise attack

explanation.surface: Someone is scared that a woman will be assaulted.
explanation.definitionFit: Being afraid of something means being fearful or frightened of it, both adjectives.

indicators.note: the words keep the answer within them, held across the join between two words

parts.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Perhaps an elderly relative has a secret boyfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is a boyfriend or male admirer, a somewhat old-fashioned word for a lover.

parts.note: the others are the rest
not so much is less

explanation.surface: Other people are calmer by comparison.
explanation.definitionFit: Restless means unable to stay still or calm, close to fidgety or agitated.

indicators.note: something designed has been arranged into a new layout, so the preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of both words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A craftsman boasts that the objects they made look true to life.
explanation.definitionFit: A realistic portrait or model closely resembles real life, so it is lifelike.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: more than usual, added
second meaning: a film performer with a non-speaking background part

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase about an additional cast member, but splits into an adjective and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for something additional and a noun for a background performer in a film crowd scene.

clue.text: Happiness of niece perhaps after dumping Republican

indicators.note: dumping means getting rid of something, so a letter is thrown out of the word

parts.note: a niece is one example of a family relative
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A niece is delighted once she has left her right-wing partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is a feeling of great joy and exhilaration, a heightened form of happiness.

wordplay.note: asks how the word election starts, answered by a short phrase about where its opening letter sits

explanation.surface: A politician asks whether this is a silly way to start a campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'how does election begin?': in an E. Run together, IN AN E is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly or senseless, and ludicrous is a synonym for absurdly foolish.

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about unsteadily, so the following letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of both words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A monk who has had too much to drink at London's main air hub.
explanation.walkthrough: A prior is the head of a priory, a monastery. Heathrow is London's largest airport; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathrow is one particular instance of an airfield for passenger flights, so it stands for the general term.

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered in order

parts.note: the letters of both words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician commended an ideal place.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is heaven or any idyllic place, an ideal existence free of trouble.

clue.text: American fellow, member of the FBI?

parts.note: A is a standard abbreviation for American
a gent, short for gentleman, is a fellow

explanation.surface: A US man is identified as working for the Federal Bureau of Investigation.
explanation.definitionFit: FBI investigators are called special agents, so an operative of the bureau is one example.

clue.text: English vehicle coming back for test of speed

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the opposite way, so the letters are read from right to left

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A British car returns home for a speed trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A race is a competition to see who is fastest, literally a contest of speed.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the 1980s stage show by Tim Rice and the ABBA songwriters
second meaning: the board game of kings, queens and pawns

explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical game' suggests musical chairs, but musical is a noun here: a stage show with that title.
explanation.definitionFit: The board game played with knights and bishops shares its name with a stage show about a Cold War tournament.

clue.text: Mull over and absorb summary of information

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to think through and take in an idea
second meaning: to break down food in the stomach and take in its nutrients

explanation.walkthrough: This is a triple definition: two verb senses and one noun sense of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers pondering news and processing a meal, while the noun is a condensed compilation or abridgement.

indicators.note: the words hold the answer inside them, spanning the gap between them

parts.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: An adversary is carrying a pilfered handgun.
explanation.definitionFit: Looted goods have been taken by theft, so they are pilfered or robbed.

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a spat is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: A never-ending quarrel takes place in a German resort town.
explanation.walkthrough: Baden-Baden is a famous German resort with thermal springs, so 'maybe' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A resort town built around mineral springs for bathing and health cures is called by this name.

indicators.note: asking what someone said points to how words are spoken, not written

parts.note: a wally is British slang for a fool, as is a nit

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether you really told a fool to come along.
explanation.walkthrough: Wally and nit are both British slang for a silly person; the silent K makes the sounds match.
explanation.definitionFit: To knit is to unite or bind together, as broken bones knit or a team is closely knit.

clue.text: Rebuke Fidel ally drinking wine with son

indicators.note: someone drinking takes a liquid inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Che Guevara fought alongside Fidel Castro in the Cuban revolution
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A Cuban revolutionary is scolded for drinking with his son.
explanation.definitionFit: To chastise is to reprimand severely, scolding someone for wrongdoing.
